title: Automated Cinematic B-Roll Generation for Content Agencies
business: Digital marketing agencies producing high-volume social media video content.
problem: High production costs and slow turnaround times when manually animating static product photography into engaging video clips.
solution: Utilizing LTX-2.5 to perform image-to-video inference, allowing agencies to animate static assets into cinematic clips using text-based motion prompts.
steps: Install the ltx-pipelines package and download the split model checkpoints.
Prepare the static source image ensuring dimensions are divisible by 32.
Execute the image-to-video inference command using the --image flag with the source path and frame index.
Apply the latent spatial upscaler to enhance the output resolution for final delivery.
outcome: Rapid, scalable production of motion-rich video assets from existing static image libraries without requiring manual animation.
limitation: The model may fail to generate videos that match the prompt perfectly, requiring iterative prompt engineering to ensure visual adherence.

diagram.description: The flow from static input to rendered video output.

code.content:
# Example of triggering image-to-video inference
# --image path/to/image.jpg 0 1.0 sets the first frame as conditioning
# --prompt defines the cinematic motion
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["python", "-m", "ltx_pipelines.distilled", "--image", "input.jpg", "0", "1.0", "--prompt", "Wind blowing through trees", "--output-path", "output.mp4"])
